title: Soil carbon sequestration verification at scale
bottleneck: Paying farmers to store carbon in soil requires measuring changes of a few tenths of a percent against huge, heterogeneous background stocks — a signal near the detection limit of affordable sampling. Models fill the gap but are poorly validated across soil types and climates, and stored carbon can be re-released by a single tillage event or drought. Additionality is equally murky: many credited practices were already spreading.
why_it_blocks: Agricultural soils could theoretically sequester gigatonnes while improving fertility, making this the most co-beneficial CDR pathway. Unverifiable claims risk turning soil carbon into a greenwashing machine that pays for business as usual.
current_state: Remote sensing, spectroscopy, and better biogeochemical models are improving MRV, and several large programs now pay for modeled outcomes. But per-field verification cheap enough for smallholders — where most of the potential lies — does not yet exist.
